finding: The TypeScript measure stops with exit 1 on a function expression that is the value of an object key, such as `first: function (n) { ... }`, so crap-score exits 2 and the story is blocked as `gate cannot measure`. The ESLint rule `complexity` reports such a function at its key, which lies before the range that the rule crap/range records for the function. pairFunctions then finds no single owner and throws "the complexity at line 2 pairs with no single function". The measure ignores GATE_SCOPE, so one such function in any kept .ts file blocks every story of the repository, also a story that changes only Python. Reproduction: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-matthiasdaues-Documents-datenschoenheit-agent-factory/89fd1670-49e4-4a59-97db-e1035150aa04/scratchpad/st0449-review/repro_typescript.sh <command> property-function. Fix: in the rule crap/range, take the parent Property as the outer node also when its value is a FunctionExpression with kind init, as for a method. Add the case to CG-13-IT-02.
why_this_severity: The command exists only on the story branch. The current TypeScript code has no such function, because the setup run measured it, and the measure stops loudly instead of reporting a wrong row (no to fails_purpose). The first story that adds the pattern gets a blocked run whose message does not name the cause.
